reviewerDerivedProposition: Five weeks of negligible intake in a client at BMI 17.1 followed by carbohydrate-containing parenteral nutrition, then a simultaneous fall in phosphorus, potassium and magnesium within the expected early window, is refeeding syndrome. The mechanism is insulin-mediated intracellular shifting of those three ions when total body stores are already depleted. The rising glucose is a concurrent parenteral-nutrition complication that requires treatment but does not explain the electrolyte triad, and a catheter infection is not supported at this point because the client is afebrile and the insertion site is benign.
requiredFacts: Five weeks of negligible intake, BMI 17.1, 11 kg loss, and the high-risk refeeding assessment - baseline_record.
The simultaneous declines - K 3.5 to 3.1, phosphorus 2.8 to 1.8, magnesium 1.8 to 1.4 - and glucose 198 rising to 204 - stage_1 ONLY.
The benign PICC site and absence of fever at this point, which defeat the infection option - stage_1.
Nothing in stage_2 or stage_3 is required.
disclosureEvidence: The disclosure is in the always-visible parent TITLE, which reads 'Refeeding syndrome during parenteral nutrition initiation in a malnourished post-operative client' and in Chinese '营养不良术后患者开始肠外营养时发生再喂养综合征'. Keyed dropdown d1 asks the learner to identify refeeding syndrome; the title names it, in both languages, and asserts it as already occurring. A title is a global surface rendered at every boundary, so no anchor reaches it. Hiding stage_2 and stage_3 is separately necessary, since stage_2 brings severe organ dysfunction and stage_3 the treatment response.
clinicalVerdict: All three keys are correct and the cloze is well built, with every blank agreeing with one pathophysiologic chain as its own strategy requires. Keyed d2 is the correct mechanism: carbohydrate delivery raises insulin, which drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly in a depleted client. Keyed d3 is the discriminating blank and is right - the hyperglycaemia is real and needs treatment but cannot explain a simultaneous three-ion fall, and the alternative that it is the primary cause inverts the causal direction. The infection distractor in d1 is properly defeated at Stage 1 by the absence of fever and the benign site, which the case establishes explicitly rather than leaving to inference. THE DEFECT IS THE TITLE, NOT THE CLINICAL CONTENT. Note that the baseline's own high-risk refeeding ASSESSMENT is legitimate and must be retained: identifying a client as high risk is the nutrition consult's documented judgement and is different from the title asserting that the syndrome has occurred.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: the bilingual parent title names the keyed diagnosis of dropdown d1 and states it as an accomplished fact.

SIBLING SURFACE, AND THE REASON A TITLE FIX IS NOT SUFFICIENT: I surveyed every sibling. All five - q1, q3, q4, q5 and q6 - contain 'refeeding' in their own text, and q3's and q4's stems and rationales name refeeding syndrome directly. Under P23 a case study is one top-level question with one aggregate submit and true unfolding reveal is deferred, so all parts render together and a learner answering q2 can read the diagnosis off sibling parts even after the title is neutralised.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, clozeStem, all nine dropdown options, all three keys, rationale, three byChoice entries and strategy are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The title discloses equally in both languages, so the repair is bilingual.
sourcesChecked: No external fetch was load-bearing for this row. The mechanism keyed in d2 is standard refeeding pathophysiology and is not contested; the discriminating judgement in d3 rests on the internal fact that a single hyperglycaemia cannot produce a simultaneous three-ion decline, and the infection exclusion rests on the absence of fever and the benign site documented in stage_1, which I read directly.
siblingImpact: HIGH. The title is a global surface visible to all six parts, and the sibling survey above shows the disclosure is distributed across the parent rather than confined to the title. Siblings q1 and q6 are non-residual and already accepted, so any edit reaching them is a change to accepted content requiring its own review.
repairConstraints: Neutralise the bilingual parent title so it does not name the syndrome - for example a title about nutrition initiation after prolonged poor intake. Apply in EN and ZH.
RETAIN the baseline nutrition consult's high-risk refeeding assessment; it is legitimate authored clinical judgement and removing it would strip the case of its reason for the monitoring plan.

Recognise that the title fix alone does NOT close the disclosure. Either re-scope q2 so it no longer asks the learner to name the syndrome and instead assesses the mechanism and the glucose interpretation, which is confined to the residual row and is my recommendation, or neutralise the diagnosis wording across the sibling parts, which touches accepted content and needs its own review.
Preserve all three dropdown keys and all nine option texts.
Anchor to stage_1 after repair.
criticalNote: This is the THIRD parent in this review whose title states the answer to one of its own parts, after the postpartum preeclampsia and clozapine parents. Two of the three - this one and preeclampsia - additionally have the diagnosis restated in sibling parts, so a rename is insufficient in both. Only the clozapine parent was safely rename-only. I recommend the integration seat treat diagnostic titles as a class and run a whole-parent surface survey for each, rather than patching row-wise.
agreementReasoning: I noticed the diagnostic title while reading the parent and derived stage_1 independently; Codex names the same defect, proposes the same boundary, correctly instructs that the legitimate baseline high-risk assessment be retained, and asks for sibling effects to be reviewed. I performed that survey and it returns the finding that changes the repair: the diagnosis appears in all five siblings, so title neutralisation is necessary but not sufficient. I supply the confined alternative route and the cross-parent pattern across the three title cases.

reviewerDerivedProposition: At Stage 2 the electrolyte derangement is no longer a laboratory abnormality but an active cause of organ failure - frequent premature ventricular contractions and a prolonged QT interval on telemetry, shallow respirations with proximal weakness severe enough that she cannot lift her arms, and a fall in orientation - against phosphorus 1.3, potassium 2.9 and magnesium 1.3 that kept falling through a first round of repletion. That carries near-term risk of lethal dysrhythmia and respiratory failure and is the priority. The new purulent PICC site is genuinely concerning and needs cultures and antibiotics in parallel, the hyperglycaemia needs coverage, and the fever needs a source rather than an antipyretic, but none of those is the proximate threat.
requiredFacts: The Stage 2 laboratory values and their failure to respond to the first repletion round - stage_2.
The cardiac, respiratory and neurological findings - stage_2 telemetry with frequent PVCs and prolonged QT, shallow effort with bibasilar decrease, lethargy, proximal weakness.
The PICC site change with purulent drainage and T 38.2, which make distractor q3_B a serious rather than a straw-man alternative - stage_2.
disclosureEvidence: stage_2 presents the competing problems without ranking them. Hiding stage_3 is necessary: stage_3 opens by recording that the provider was notified urgently of 'continued electrolyte decline despite repletion, cardiac rhythm changes, respiratory compromise, and PICC-site findings' and then lists the ordered response, which both ranks the problems and supplies the sibling rows' answers.
clinicalVerdict: The key is correct - the electrolyte-driven cardiorespiratory compromise is the immediate threat - and the distractors are well chosen, with q3_B in particular being a real competing diagnosis rather than filler. TWO DEFECTS. FIRST, a shared-surface chronology impossibility that I verified by arithmetic: the PICC is placed in stage_1 at 18 hours post-operatively; stage_2 is at 30 hours post-operatively and states 'The dressing was changed 24 hours ago per protocol', which places the dressing change at 6 hours post-operatively, twelve hours BEFORE the line existed. SECOND, the rationale overstates causal certainty. It says the PICC findings do 'not explain the established electrolyte triad or current rhythm instability', which is true of the electrolytes but too strong about the rhythm and the systemic picture: this client has T 38.2, HR 118, BP 98/58 and RR 22 with purulent drainage from a central line, so infection may well be coexisting and contributing, and the correct teaching is that the electrolyte problem is treated first while infection is evaluated in parallel, not that infection is excluded as a contributor.
contentDefects: PRIMARY, SHARED SURFACE: impossible PICC dressing chronology in stage_2, as computed above. Affects residual rows q3, q4 and q5, all of which are anchored at stage_2.
SECONDARY: the key rationale and the q3_B rationale assert more causal separation than the findings support. Soften to parallel evaluation rather than exclusion.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, four options, key, rationale, four byChoice entries and strategy are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The chronology error is in the shared stage_2 exhibit and is reproduced in Chinese, so both corrections are bilingual.
sourcesChecked: Sepsis management guidance (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430939/) - read directly; confirms at least two sets of blood cultures prior to antibiotics with broad-spectrum antibiotics within one hour, which underwrites the parallel-evaluation framing and is the same source relied on for the sibling rows. The chronology finding rests on arithmetic over the stage headings and exhibit text in the frozen packet.
siblingImpact: HIGH AND SHARED WITH TWO OTHER RESIDUAL ROWS. The chronology correction lives in the stage_2 exhibit, which is the boundary stage for residual rows q3, q4 AND q5. Apply once as a single coordinated edit and re-review the three parts together. Non-residual siblings q1 and q6 are baseline-anchored and cannot see stage_2.
repairConstraints: Correct the PICC dressing chronology in stage_2 in EN and ZH using an explicitly reviewed timeline consistent with a line placed at 18 hours and a Stage 2 at 30 hours. Apply ONCE for rows q3, q4 and q5.

Soften the causal language in the key rationale and the q3_B rationale: the electrolyte decline strongly supports urgent correction, while infection may coexist or contribute and requires timely parallel evaluation.
Do not alter the key or the four option texts; the prioritisation is correct.
Anchor to stage_2 after repair.
criticalNote: As in the lateral-incivility parent, one shared stage_2 edit serves three residual rows here. Treating them independently risks duplicate or conflicting corrections to the same exhibit.
agreementReasoning: I derived stage_2 independently and confirmed Codex's chronology finding by recomputing it from the stage headings rather than accepting it. Codex names both defects - the causal overstatement and the impossible line timeline - and proposes the same boundary. I add the specific arithmetic, the observation that the client's vital signs make the infection contribution a live possibility rather than a theoretical one, and the coordination requirement across the three rows sharing stage_2.

reviewerDerivedProposition: The nurse escalates urgently with the full picture, anticipates reducing the caloric load rather than independently stopping a high-dextrose infusion, gives the higher-tier potassium, phosphate and magnesium repletion under continuous cardiac monitoring, and obtains paired cultures before the first vancomycin dose. Treating the glucose aggressively with insulin ahead of the potassium would drive potassium further intracellularly and worsen the very derangement causing the dysrhythmia.
requiredFacts: The Stage 2 values, the failed first repletion round and the organ findings - stage_2.

The unit electrolyte replacement protocol defining the higher tier - baseline_record, which gives KCl 40 mEq for K below 3.0, sodium phosphate 30 mmol for phosphorus below 1.5, and magnesium sulfate 2 g for magnesium below 1.5. I checked that the Stage 2 values (K 2.9, phosphorus 1.3, magnesium 1.3) all fall in those bands, so 'higher-tier' is derivable from baseline plus stage_2 without needing stage_3.
The PICC site findings motivating cultures - stage_2.
disclosureEvidence: stage_2 supplies the deterioration but no plan. Hiding stage_3 is ESSENTIAL: stage_3 lists the actual orders - reduce TPN by 50 percent without abrupt discontinuation, higher-tier repletion, cultures from PICC and periphery before vancomycin, increased glucose monitoring - which is keyed options q4_B, q4_C and q4_D stated as accomplished orders.
clinicalVerdict: The four keyed actions are correct and both distractors are genuinely and instructively wrong, with q4_F teaching a real and dangerous error - insulin ahead of potassium correction. I specifically examined Codex's caution about a universal prohibition on stopping parenteral nutrition and find it already addressed in the text: distractor q4_E is conditioned as stopping TPN 'without a provider order or dextrose/glucose-monitoring backup plan', and its rationale repeats the qualifier, so the item does not teach that prescribed cessation is never appropriate. That concern therefore needs no change. THE DEFECTS ARE THE SHARED stage_2 CHRONOLOGY ERROR identified on row q3, and an unconditional culture-before-antibiotic instruction. Keyed option q4_D reads 'Draw blood cultures from the PICC and a peripheral site before starting the first ordered vancomycin dose' with no qualifier. Verified that at least two sets of blood cultures are recommended prior to antibiotics but that broad-spectrum antibiotics are to be given within one hour, so cultures must not substantially delay treatment. This client is febrile at 38.2 with hypotension, tachycardia and purulent central-line drainage, which is precisely the situation where an absolute culture-first rule could delay time-critical therapy.
contentDefects: INHERITED, SHARED SURFACE: the impossible PICC dressing chronology in stage_2.

PRIMARY: keyed option q4_D states the culture-before-antibiotic sequence unconditionally, without the qualifier that antibiotics must not be materially delayed if cultures cannot be obtained promptly.
CHECKED AND CLEARED: the parenteral-nutrition cessation option is already properly conditioned and does not assert a universal prohibition.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, six options, key, rationale, six byChoice entries and strategy are semantically equivalent EN/ZH, including the conditional clauses in distractor q4_E. The unconditional culture wording is unconditional in both languages, so the repair is bilingual.
sourcesChecked: Sepsis management guidance (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430939/) - read directly. Confirms 'At least two sets of blood cultures are recommended prior to administration of antibiotics' alongside 'Broad-spectrum antibiotics within one hour of diagnosis for all patients', establishing that cultures precede antibiotics but must not substantially delay them. This is the basis for the qualifier.
Internal check of the baseline replacement protocol against the Stage 2 values to confirm the higher tier is derivable without stage_3.
siblingImpact: HIGH AND SHARED. The chronology correction is the SAME stage_2 edit required by rows q3 and q5. The culture-wording correction is confined to this row's option q4_D, but it should be made consistently with the parallel correction in sibling row q5's timing columns.
repairConstraints: Apply the shared stage_2 chronology correction specified on row q3 once, in EN and ZH, for all three residual rows.
Qualify keyed option q4_D and its byChoice rationale so the culture-first instruction is conditional on prompt collection without material treatment delay. Keep the option keyed correct.
Make this qualification consistent with the corresponding change to sibling row q5's timing columns.
Do not change distractor q4_E; it is already correctly conditioned.
Preserve the key q4_A through q4_D.
Anchor to stage_2 after repair.
criticalNote: The culture-timing wording is the one place in this parent where a clinically correct principle is stated so absolutely that following it could cause harm in the very scenario the case depicts.
agreementReasoning: I derived stage_2 independently and reached the same two live concerns Codex raises - the shared chronology error and the culture-before-antibiotic conditionality - verifying the latter against sepsis guidance rather than the registry pointer. I differ on one of Codex's three points: its instruction to avoid a universal prohibition on prescribed parenteral-nutrition cessation describes a defect this item does not have, since the option and its rationale are already conditioned on the absence of an order and a backup plan. I record that as checked and cleared rather than carrying it forward as required work, so the producer seat is not sent to fix something that is already correct. I also verified that the higher-tier repletion is derivable from baseline plus stage_2, which is what keeps the boundary at stage_2 rather than forcing stage_3.

reviewerDerivedProposition: Among the received orders, reducing the caloric load and giving the higher-tier repletion address the mechanism and the active dysrhythmia and respiratory risk, so neither waits on the infection workup. Paired cultures are time-critical because they precede the first antibiotic dose, and the vancomycin follows them. Increased glucose monitoring with sliding-scale coverage is ongoing supportive management that must not displace the acute electrolyte actions.
requiredFacts: The Stage 2 clinical state justifying the urgency ranking - stage_2.

The orders themselves, WHICH ARE A PROBLEM. The stem says 'At Stage 2, orders have been received', and each of the five rows restates its order, so the item is self-carrying. But the orders are documented ONLY in the stage_3 exhibit, which retrospectively narrates 'At Stage 2, the provider was notified urgently ... Orders: reduce TPN rate by 50% ...'. At a stage_2 boundary the chart the learner can see contains no such orders.
The baseline replacement protocol, which lets the learner confirm the higher tier - baseline_record.
disclosureEvidence: stage_3 both states the orders and reports their outcome, so leaving it visible would supply the premise and confirm the sequencing. Hiding it is necessary. The residual awkwardness is the mirror image: with stage_3 hidden, the orders the stem asserts have been received appear nowhere in the visible chart, and exist only in the stem's assertion and the rows' own restatement.
clinicalVerdict: The timing ranking is clinically sound and the four columns are, unusually for this population, genuinely distinct timing categories rather than overlapping labels - I checked for the false-exclusivity defect that converted several other matrices in this review and it is absent, so single_per_row is appropriate here. THE DEFECT IS THAT TWO COLUMNS STATE THE CULTURE-ANTIBIOTIC RELATIONSHIP ABSOLUTELY. Column q5_c2 reads 'Must occur before the first antibiotic dose' and column q5_c3 reads 'Give only after cultures are obtained'. Verified against sepsis guidance that cultures are recommended prior to antibiotics but that broad-spectrum antibiotics are to be given within one hour, so the sequence is a strong default rather than an absolute bar. In a client who is febrile at 38.2 with a blood pressure of 98/58, a rate of 118 and purulent central-line drainage, a learner taught that vancomycin may be given 'only after' cultures could defensibly withhold a time-critical antibiotic if cultures prove difficult to draw. Separately, the row set depends on orders documented only in a hidden stage, as recorded above.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: columns q5_c2 and q5_c3 state the culture-before-antibiotic relationship as absolute, without preserving prompt treatment where cultures cannot be obtained without significant delay.

SECONDARY, PLACEMENT: the Stage 2 orders that all five rows act on are narrated only inside the stage_3 exhibit. My numeric-dependency screen flagged this row on the value 50, which appears in row q5_r1 and in stage_3 but nowhere in the visible prefix. The rows restate their own orders so the item remains answerable, but the chart and the stem disagree about where the orders live.
INHERITED, SHARED SURFACE: the impossible PICC dressing chronology in stage_2.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, four column labels, five rows, the key and the rationale are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The absolute wording of the two timing columns is equally absolute in Chinese ('必须在首次抗生素前完成' and '仅在抽取培养后给予'), so the repair is bilingual.
sourcesChecked: Sepsis management guidance (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430939/) - read directly, as for the sibling q4 row: cultures prior to antibiotics, antibiotics within one hour, and the principle that antimicrobial administration must not be substantially delayed by collection. This is what makes the absolute column wording unsafe.
Internal trace of the order text across the stage_2 and stage_3 exhibits to establish the placement problem.
siblingImpact: HIGH AND SHARED. The chronology correction is the SAME stage_2 edit required by rows q3 and q4, and the culture-timing qualification must be made consistently with the corresponding change to sibling row q4's option q4_D. Non-residual siblings q1 and q6 are baseline-anchored and unaffected.
repairConstraints: Revise columns q5_c2 and q5_c3 and the matching rationale in EN and ZH so they preserve prompt antibiotic treatment if cultures cannot be obtained without significant delay, rather than stating an absolute bar.
Make this consistent with the qualification applied to sibling row q4's option q4_D.

After the wording change, re-check that each row still maps to exactly one column, since widening the timing language could make q5_c1 and the revised q5_c3 both defensible for the vancomycin row. Codex asks for this re-check and I endorse it.

Resolve the placement problem: either move the Stage 2 orders into the stage_2 exhibit where the stem says they were received, or reword the stem so it does not assert that orders are already in hand at a point where the visible chart contains none.
Apply the shared stage_2 chronology correction once, coordinated with rows q3 and q4.
Anchor to stage_2 after repair.
criticalNote: This row carries the only remaining structural oddity in the parent: the item is set at Stage 2 but acts on an order set the case documents in Stage 3. It is answerable because the rows restate the orders, which is why I do not hold the row, but the chart placement should be fixed rather than relied upon.
agreementReasoning: I derived stage_2 independently and reached Codex's two main points independently - the absolute culture and antibiotic timing columns, and the shared line chronology - verifying the timing principle against sepsis guidance. I endorse Codex's instruction to re-check selection-mode uniqueness after the wording repair, which is a genuinely sharp observation, and I confirm by inspection that the columns are currently disjoint so the risk arises only from the repair itself. I add the placement finding, which my own numeric-dependency screen surfaced and which neither Campaign-16 seat nor Codex records: all five rows act on orders that the case documents only in the hidden stage.
